title: PAGEANT TO START AT 6PM

title: SENTENCED FOR DEATH
full_story:
A Columbus, Indiana man was sentenced to 20 years in prison for the July 6, 2025 DUI death of 29-year-old Braden Christopher Robertson of Fairfield.

Jerrin Alan Staker, 44, entered a guilty plea Monday in Johnson County, Indiana Superior Court to a felony charge of driving intoxicated causing death with a habitual offender enhancement.

The crash happened in Franklin, Indiana.  Witnesses reported that Staker was driving a Jeep south at 100 mph, swerving through traffic and running traffic lights.  Staker ran a red light and hit Robertson’s Volkswagen Jetta.  Before the crash, Staker drove in a turn lane and on the shoulder of the road to avoid vehicles stopped at the red light.  An investigation revealed drug paraphernalia inside the Jeep.  Further testing revealed Staker had high levels of both methamphetamine and fentanyl in his system.

At sentencing, Robertson’s mother, Jennifer Robertson of Cisne spoke of her son’s character and his legacy as an organ donor.

Braden Robertson had only lived in Franklin for about a month, he had worked at Harr’s Ace Hardware in Flora and later worked at Hadwell Hardware in Franklin, Indiana.

title: JOHNSONVILLE COMMUNITY DAYS
full_story:
Johnsonville Community Days sponsored by the Johnsonville Ruritan Club will start tonight.  This year’s theme is “Red, White and Rural.

At 6:30 pm there will be the Truck and Tractor pull, admission is $10 with a $25 hook fee.  There will also be Bingo at 6:30 pm and sandwiches and drinks will be available at the pavilion.

Tomorrow’s events will include the Flea Market and Craft Fair, 5K, with registration at 6:15 am, and the run walk at 7 am.  The car truck motorcycle and tractor show registration runs from 9 – Noon.  There is a $15 entry fee, for cars, trucks and motorcycles, tractors are free.  There will also be a parade on Saturday with lineup at 9:30 and the parade at 10 am with Harlan Allison as this year’s parade marshal.  At 11, Ham & Beans will be available in the Ruritan building, and a mud bog will start.  At 3:30 the Little Miss and Mister Johnsonville pageant registration will start for those age 3 to 10.  The pageant will begin at 4 pm.  The fish and chicken supper is at 5, and the pedal pull is at 6 pm, and the Kids Power Wheels pull will be at 7 pm.

To enter the car, truck, motorcycle, and tractor show call Lawrence Pennington at 618-919-0297.  To enter the Parade call Ellen Sitze at 618-919-0884 and to enter the mud bog call Kody Payne at 618-383-5883.  To enter the Little Miss and Mister contest call Rachel Johnson at 618-231-1568.

The event wraps up on Sunday with the Community Church service with speaker Travis Mix at 10:30 and the fried chicken meal is at noon.

title: BACK TO SCHOOL VACCINE CLINICS
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is having a series of Back-to-School vaccine clinics.

The next clinic is on Monday, from 8:30 am to 6 pm at the Health Department on 12th Street.  Appointments are not necessary but are appreciated.  Appointments can be made by calling 618-662-4406.

Illinois state law requires certain immunizations for children and adults enrolled in childcare, school, or college.  State law also mandates immunizations for adults in specific fields of work.

There will also be Clinics on Thursday, August 6th, Wednesday, August 12th, and Thursday, August 13th from 8:30 am to 6 pm.  The final clinic will be from Friday, August 14th from 8 am to Noon.

Again, appointments are not necessary, but appreciated, if you have questions call the Clay County Health Department at 618-662-4406.

title: 4H HALL OF FAME
full_story:
Illinois Extension in Clay, Wayne and Richland Counties have nominated their 2026 inductees into the Illinois 4-H Hall of Fame.

Counties are welcome to nominate individuals, or couples, who meet the award criteria annually, but are not required to do so.  The following inductees were selected for their outstanding contributions to their county 4-H programs in Clay, Wayne and Richland Counties.

In Clay County Rocky and Anita Allen have been devoted supporters of Clay County 4‑H, generously giving their time and talents to strengthen the program and positively impact local youth.  As longtime leaders of the All Around Gang 4‑H Club, they guided members in projects and activities while inspiring participation across generations, including their own grandchildren.  Rocky has also served as rabbit and poultry superintendent, mentoring exhibitors and helping them build skills and confidence.

In Wayne County Shannon and Travis Mix spent nine years leading the 4-H Country Club before retiring as leaders last year.  Their passion for supporting 4-H members and leadership through example shone through during their time as volunteers.  “Their service has strengthened our program, expanded opportunities for youth, and fostered a positive, welcoming 4‑H community,” said Ryan Littlejohn, Wayne County 4-H program coordinator.

In Richland County, Lora Kocher, is a former 4-H member and a third-generation club leader.  She is very involved in her community and has a full-time career yet still finds time to volunteer as the Country Clovers club leader for nine years and counting.  Those who have worked with her note that she is passionate about 4-H, dependable, and always willing to help.

Inductees will be recognized at a ceremony during their county exhibit day at the Illinois State Fair on August 15th, in Springfield.  To learn more about the Illinois 4-H Hall of Fame inductees, past and present, visit 4h.extension.illinois.edu/awards/4-h-hall-fame

title: MURDER CHARGES
full_story:
Dalewayne Turner’s wife and half-brother have each been charged with three counts of first degree murder in Will County.

Turner’s dismembered body was found in Lake Mattoon in at the end of June.  26-year-old James Adams and 62-year-old Robin Turner had already been charged with concealment of a homicide and dismembering a human body.  A Will County grand jury has now indicted the two suspects with Dalewayne Turner’s murder, alleging that the murder occurred at Turner’s home in Plainfield and involved sharp force injury.

Robin Turner is next due in court on Monday, while James Adams’ next appearance will be September 10th.  Both are being held in custody.

title: FRESH BENEFIT
full_story:
Governor JB Pritzker and the Illinois Department of Human Services announced people in Illinois who lost their Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits will get a one-time $400 benefit per eligible household member through the new Families Receiving Emergency Support for Hunger (FRESH) program.

This $70 million program was enacted as part of the Governor’s FY27 budget.

Approximately 100,000 Illinoisans will get a one-time benefit beginning August 1st, and IDHS will provide funding each month to more people who lose coverage until funding is exhausted.

The State of Illinois has worked with people to help them regain access to food assistance, but nearly 100,000 people are without SNAP benefits.  They will be receiving support from the FRESH Program this week.

Households with newly eligible members will be issued one-time FRESH benefits after the 16th of the month in which they lose access to SNAP until funding is exhausted.

title: DISASTER LOAN OUTREACH CENTERS
full_story:
The Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security, in partnership with the US Small Business Administration (SBA) and local municipalities, is promoting multiple Disaster Loan Outreach Centers (DLOCs) to assist residents and businesses impacted by the severe storms on June 10th, 11th and 17th.  These disaster declarations cover the primary counties of Cook and LaSalle for the June 10th, 11th storms and Coles and Effingham for the June 17th storms.  Residents and businesses in the contiguous counties are also eligible for SBA disaster assistance, including Clay, Clark, Cumberland, Douglas, Edgar, Fayette, Jasper, Moultrie, and Shelby Counties for the June 17th storms.  Centers will provide in person support for applicants seeking low interest disaster loans for storm related damages not covered by insurance.

SBA customer service representatives will staff each center to answer questions, explain the application process, and assist individuals and businesses in completing applications.  Walk-ins are welcome at all sites.  Residents and business owners in SBA declared disaster counties and counties that border those counties are eligible to apply and may visit any Disaster Loan Outreach Centers, regardless of where they live.

In Effingham County the Outreach Center will be at the Effingham School District Building at 2803 S. Banker St, and will be open Monday through Friday from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm and Saturday from 10:00 am to 2:00 pm.  For online applications, visit sba.gov/disaster.  Applicants may also call SBA’s Customer Service Center at 800-659-2955 or email [email protected].  People who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability may dial 7-1-1 for relay services.

Homeowners can apply for up to $500,000 in low-interest SBA disaster loans to repair or replace damaged or destroyed real estate.  Homeowners or renters can apply for up to $100,000 to repair or replace damaged or destroyed personal property.  Businesses and not-for-profits can borrow up to $2 million for physical damages.  For more information, visit https://www.sba.gov/funding-programs/disaster-assistance.

In addition to the primary counties declared under this disaster, residents and businesses located in contiguous counties are also eligible to apply for SBA disaster assistance.  The deadline to submit SBA disaster loan applications for physical property damage is September 8th, and the deadline to submit applications for economic injury is April 12th, 2027.
